transcript.content: Hi, welcome in. I'm Dr. [Name]. To start, can you tell me what brings you in to see me today?

Hi, Doctor. Well, I guess what brings me in is... I've been having these times where I just eat, and after I do it, I just sit there looking at all the empty containers. I feel really disgusted with myself. I've always tried to be a steady, in-control man. But when I'm sitting there looking at what I just did, I feel like I'm not that guy at all.
After one of these eating episodes, do you ever try to get rid of the food or make up for it—like making yourself vomit, using laxatives, fasting, or exercising a lot?

No, I... no, I don't do any of that. I don't try to throw it up or take laxatives or anything like that. And with my job driving all day, I definitely don't exercise to make up for it. I just kind of sit there with it, feeling awful.
How often would you say these episodes of eating and feeling out of control happen—like, how many times a week or month?

Well, since I've been stuck at home with this back injury... it's been happening a lot more. I'd say it happens several nights most weeks. Honestly, I can't think of a single week in the last three months where I didn't have at least one of those episodes. It's pretty constant right now.
During these episodes, would you say you're eating a much larger amount of food in a short period of time than most people would eat in similar circumstances?

Yeah, definitely. I mean... some evenings I’ll heat up what I swear is just going to be one bowl of pozole. But before I know it, I’ve gone through the whole pot. Then I'm eating a couple of tamales, chips, and whatever other leftovers are just sitting there in the fridge. It's like I’m feeding a whole crew instead of just myself. So, yeah, it's a lot of food in a short amount of time.
